audits.title: Improving management of asthma: closing the loop or progressing along the audit spiral?
audits.standard: Checklist of important aspects of acute asthma management
audits.setting: Large city teaching hospital (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)

cycle1.result: Oral corticosteroids 69 (68%); oxygen 62 (61%).

audits.other_findings: Intermediate 1985-6 survey (85 patients): corticosteroids 67 (79%), oxygen 51 (60%).
audits.citation: Bucknall CE, Robertson C, Moran F, Stevenson RD. Improving management of asthma: closing the loop or progressing along the audit spiral?. Qual Health Care. 1992;1(1):15-20. doi:10.1136/qshc.1.1.15. PMID: 10136823.

audits.title: Are doctors still failing to assess and treat asthma attacks? An audit of the management of acute attacks in a health district.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society asthma guidelines
audits.setting: Primary and secondary care in Canterbury and Thanet District

cycle1.result: Peak flow recorded in 234 (76% of those aged 6 or over); emergency bronchodilation in 114 (30%); systemic steroids in 204 (54%); oxygen not used in primary care.

audits.other_findings: Of 28 life-threatening attacks, oxygen used in only two and only six (21%) referred for admission.
audits.citation: Pinnock H, Johnson A, Young P, Martin N. Are doctors still failing to assess and treat asthma attacks? An audit of the management of acute attacks in a health district. Respir Med. 1999;93(6):397-401. doi:10.1053/rmed.1999.0575. PMID: 10464821.

audits.title: A criterion based audit of inpatient asthma care. Closing the feedback loop.
audits.standard: Hospital asthma management protocol: PEF variability 20% or less before discharge and written check of inhaler technique
audits.setting: Specialist respiratory ward, West Norwich Hospital

cycle1.result: PEF variability criterion met in 30/55 (54%); written inhaler technique check 32/55.

audits.intervention: PEF discharge criterion relaxed in line with national guidelines, a stamp introduced to record inhaler technique checks, and encouragement from senior staff.

cycle2.result: PEF variability criterion met in 17/23 (74%); written inhaler technique check 22/23 (96%).

audits.other_findings: Across both periods (78 patients) 65 of 68 local patients were seen in chest clinic within six weeks.
audits.citation: Lim KL, Harrison BD. A criterion based audit of inpatient asthma care. Closing the feedback loop. J R Coll Physicians Lond. 1992;26(1):71-75. PMID: 1315391.

audits.title: An audit of acute asthma admissions to a respiratory unit.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society acute asthma guidelines
audits.setting: Specialist respiratory unit, King's Cross Hospital, Dundee

cycle1.result: PEFR recorded 52%, blood gases 72%, speech 27%, air entry 58%, exhaustion 4%; 93% of severe cases given corticosteroids but none given more than 35% oxygen; chest radiograph 87%, serum potassium 56%.

audits.intervention: Severity marker stamp for case notes and treatment guidelines implemented.
audits.other_findings: 78% had at least three of five objective markers of acute severe asthma.
audits.citation: Lipworth BJ, Jackson CM, Ziyaie D, Winter JH, Dhillon PD, Clark RA. An audit of acute asthma admissions to a respiratory unit. Health Bull (Edinb). 1992;50(5):389-398. PMID: 1399586.

audits.title: Hearing half the message? A re-audit of the care of patients with acute asthma by emergency ambulance crews in London.
audits.standard: Service treatment protocols aligned with British Thoracic Society acute asthma guidelines
audits.setting: London Ambulance Service, catchment of four hospitals

cycle1.result: Some under-recognition and under-treatment of severe asthma; poor documentation of on-scene condition; 58% of A&E-diagnosed asthma patients given nebulised salbutamol by crew.

audits.intervention: Protocols widened in line with BTS guidelines, results disseminated and training for all operational staff

cycle2.result: 75% of A&E-diagnosed asthma patients given nebulised salbutamol; 43 asthma patients untreated; protocol adherence high.

audits.other_findings: Pre-hospital documentation of key observations did not improve; salbutamol given to more non-asthma patients (15 to 161).
audits.citation: Snooks H, Halter M, Palmer Y, Booth H, Moore F. Hearing half the message? A re-audit of the care of patients with acute asthma by emergency ambulance crews in London. Qual Saf Health Care. 2005;14(6):455-458. doi:10.1136/qshc.2004.012336. PMID: 16326794.

audits.title: Medical audit on asthma in an emergency department.
audits.standard: Four indicators: severity evaluation, diagnostic tests, treatment and discharge plan
audits.setting: Adult emergency department, Hospital Universitario La Fe, Valencia

cycle1.result: Respiratory rate recorded in 27%, heart rate 50%, peak flow 20%; oxygen saturation 93%; no treatment in 12%; systemic steroids in 80% of treated; 17% discharged with no change to usual treatment.

audits.other_findings: Diagnostic tests were overused (blood tests and chest radiograph in all).
audits.citation: Linares T, Campos A, Torres M, Reyes J. Medical audit on asthma in an emergency department. Allergol Immunopathol (Madr). 2006;34(6):248-251. doi:10.1157/13095872. PMID: 17173841.

audits.title: Medical audit on children with asthma in an Emergency Department.
audits.standard: 17 explicit indicators from international guides
audits.setting: Emergency Department, La Fe University Hospital, Valencia

cycle1.result: Cause of crisis recorded 32%; severity 18%; supportive treatment 24%; respiratory rate 49%; peak flow 0%; auscultation 100%; treatment result 69%.

audits.other_findings: Systemic corticosteroids given in 12%; resident documentation not signed by staff. A re-audit was proposed.

audits.title: Clinical audit: management of acute severe asthma in west Glasgow.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society acute asthma guidelines
audits.setting: Acute medical unit, Western Infirmary, Glasgow

cycle1.result: Severity documented 55%, incorrect in 33%; under-treatment 24%.

audits.other_findings: Peak flow under-recorded (72% at admission, 67% monitoring); no life-threatening attacks identified; 60% overall inappropriately treated.
audits.citation: Bayes HK, Oyeniran O, Shepherd M, Walters M. Clinical audit: management of acute severe asthma in west Glasgow. Scott Med J. 2010;55(1):6-9. doi:10.1258/rsmsmj.55.1.6. PMID: 20218271.

audits.title: Use of a guideline based questionnaire to audit hospital care of acute asthma.
audits.standard: Hospital guidelines on management of acute asthma
audits.setting: One district general hospital, Central Middlesex Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Overall deviations from guidelines in severity recording, emergency beta 2 agonists (60/76, 79%), steroids (43/76, 57%) and antibiotics per guideline (29/45, 64%).

cycle2.result: Recording of arterial blood gas tensions improved (chi 2 = 7.0, p = 0.08); few other standards improved.

audits.other_findings: Chest physicians more rigorous than general physicians in recording severity and timely steroids; overall results reported for all 76 patients.
audits.citation: Bell D, Layton AJ, Gabbay J. Use of a guideline based questionnaire to audit hospital care of acute asthma. BMJ. 1991;302(6790):1440-1443. doi:10.1136/bmj.302.6790.1440. PMID: 2070112.

audits.title: A clinical audit of the management of acute asthmatic attacks in adults and children presenting to an emergency department.
audits.standard: UHWI acute asthma management protocol and British Adult Asthma Audit Tool
audits.setting: Accident and Emergency Department, University Hospital of the West Indies, Kingston

cycle1.result: Severity assessed in 31%; PEFR recorded in 62% but pre and post PEFR in only 18.1%; nebulisation within suggested time in 4.4%; 94.2% given inhaled corticosteroid and bronchodilator prescription at discharge.

audits.other_findings: Failure to assess and document severity and under-use of PEFR were the main shortfalls.
audits.citation: Dasgupta S, Williams EW, Walters C, Eldemire-Shearer D, Williams-Johnson J. A clinical audit of the management of acute asthmatic attacks in adults and children presenting to an emergency department. West Indian Med J. 2014;63(3):226-233. doi:10.7727/wimj.2013.146. PMID: 25314279.

audits.title: Improving asthma care with Asthma-COPD Afterhours Respiratory Nurse at Emergency (A-CARE).
audits.standard: GINA guideline recommendations for ED discharge (oral and inhaled corticosteroid prescription and outpatient follow-up); target adherence 80%
audits.setting: Emergency department, Singapore General Hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline median adherence: OCS prescription 58%, ICS initiation 27%, follow-up issued 69%.

audits.intervention: After-hours asthma nurse counselling and clinical decision support service (A-CARE) in the ED three nights a week, run through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: In patients reviewed by A-CARE, median adherence: OCS prescription 86%, ICS initiation 67%, follow-up issued 92%.

audits.other_findings: Referral rate to A-CARE was only 16% in an audit of all ED asthma patients; follow-up attendance was higher with counselling (41.7% vs 15.9%, p=0.0388).
audits.citation: Chew SY, Leow JYL, Chan AKW, Chan JJ, Tan KBK, Aman B, et al.. Improving asthma care with Asthma-COPD Afterhours Respiratory Nurse at Emergency (A-CARE). BMJ Open Qual. 2020;9(2):e000894. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2019-000894. PMID: 32487527.

audits.title: An audit of the British Thoracic Society asthma discharge care bundle in a teaching hospital.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society Asthma Discharge Care Bundle
audits.setting: Teaching hospital, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, London; 12-month retrospective audit

cycle1.result: Hospital complied with the bundle overall; 85% had inhaler technique checked but 62% were given no written inhaler instructions.

audits.other_findings: Respiratory nurse specialists were more compliant with most bundle statements than the medical team; education on record-keeping recommended.
audits.citation: Awli YF, Addis G. An audit of the British Thoracic Society asthma discharge care bundle in a teaching hospital. Br J Nurs. 2021;30(13):772-779. doi:10.12968/bjon.2021.30.13.772. PMID: 34251850.

audits.title: Audit of Asthma Exacerbation Management in a Swiss General Hospital.
audits.standard: Swiss asthma guidelines and international GINA guidelines
audits.setting: Cantonal Hospital Baselland, general hospital

cycle1.result: PEF measured in 14%; SABA plus short-acting anticholinergic given to 96%; systemic glucocorticosteroids within 6 h in 55% of severe cases; reliever prescribed at discharge in 64%; new or increased ICS controller in 55%; 49% had no follow-up organised.

audits.other_findings: SpO2 and heart rate were assessed at presentation in nearly all patients. Authors recommend routine PEF measurement and intensified treatment.
audits.citation: Schnyder D, Lüthi-Corridori G, Leuppi-Taegtmeyer AB, Boesing M, Geigy N, Leuppi JD. Audit of Asthma Exacerbation Management in a Swiss General Hospital. Respiration. 2023;102(1):12-24. doi:10.1159/000527268. PMID: 36380628.

audits.title: A prospective audit of asthma management following emergency asthma treatment at a teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Published guidelines for acute and ongoing asthma management (Australian Asthma Management Plan)
audits.setting: Primary and Emergency Care Department, John Hunter Hospital, Newcastle, NSW (tertiary teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Lung function measured in 95% of acute presentations; history and examination fully documented in 28%; corticosteroids underused and ipratropium used inappropriately.

audits.other_findings: At 8-12 weeks, 46% had activity limitation and 66% impaired lung function; one-third undertreated; only 20% did peak flow monitoring and 21% recalled an exacerbation plan.
audits.citation: Gibson PG, Talbot PI, Hancock J, Hensley MJ. A prospective audit of asthma management following emergency asthma treatment at a teaching hospital. Med J Aust. 1993;158(11):775-778. doi:10.5694/j.1326-5377.1993.tb121962.x. PMID: 8341193.

audits.title: Asthma management in accident and emergency and the BTS guidelines--a study of the impact of clinical audit.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society asthma guidelines
audits.setting: Accident and Emergency Department, Guy's Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Ability to complete a sentence recorded in 63%; nebuliser given when indicated in 97%; chest x ray when indicated in 73%; blood gases in 73%.

audits.intervention: Continuous audit programme ended and most medical staff changed.

cycle2.period: April and May 1994 (one year after audit ended)
cycle2.result: Sentence recorded in 33%; nebuliser 88%; chest x ray 43%; blood gases 33%.

audits.other_findings: Care worsened once audit stopped; areas affecting asthma control after discharge fell short in both periods.
audits.citation: Stell IM. Asthma management in accident and emergency and the BTS guidelines--a study of the impact of clinical audit. J Accid Emerg Med. 1996;13(6):392-394. doi:10.1136/emj.13.6.392. PMID: 8947795.

audits.title: Reaudit of acute asthma admissions using a severity marker stamp and determinants of an outcome measure.
audits.standard: Documentation of acute asthma severity markers
audits.setting: Specialist respiratory centre, King's Cross Hospital, Dundee

cycle1.result: PEFR 52%, respiratory rate 44%, ABG 72%, air entry 58%, speech 27%, exhaustion 4%; no patient received FiO2 >0.35.

audits.intervention: Severity marker stamp in case notes.

cycle2.result: PEFR 83%, respiratory rate 81%, ABG 80%, air entry 86%, speech 86%, exhaustion 86% (p = 0.001 to 0.04); 66% received FiO2 0.60.

audits.other_findings: Mean admission five days; time for pulse to fall to 80/min best predicted length of stay.

audits.title: National asthma attack audit 1991-2. General Practitioners in Asthma Group.
audits.standard: Recommended asthma guidelines
audits.setting: 218 general practices

cycle1.result: 1546 (86%) managed in general practice, 225 (12%) admitted; underuse of nebulised bronchodilators and systemic steroids at all severities.

audits.other_findings: Step up in maintenance therapy after an attack was often not done; recording of clinical data variable.

audits.title: Does participation in distance learning and audit improve the care of patients with acute asthma attacks? The General Practitioners in Asthma Group.
audits.standard: Recommended asthma management guidelines
audits.setting: General practices across the UK (General Practitioners in Asthma Group)

cycle1.result: Nebulised bronchodilators 272 (35%); systemic steroids 563 (72%); step-up in preventive therapy 402 (51%).

audits.intervention: Distance learning programme and personalised audit feedback.
audits.other_findings: 91 GPs completed the cycle; motivated GPs may self-select into audit.
audits.citation: Hoskins G, Neville RG, Smith B, Clark RA. Does participation in distance learning and audit improve the care of patients with acute asthma attacks? The General Practitioners in Asthma Group. Health Bull (Edinb). 1997;55(3):150-155. PMID: 9364102.
